intention: Place the charter tool instance under codemonkey — first code ownership transfer from CC to another device. Charter is a building tool; build-quality feedback belongs to the builder. Creates the instance address (devices/codemonkey/0/tools/charter/0/), wires bus routing so 'charter' resolves to the held instance, and attaches a data_recorder backpack so the instance collects feedback for a sleep-state LLM reader.
why: Surfaced by undelivered bus message (0bfd6e268f73): charter self-addressed a node_class census finding to 'charter' flat, which has no receiver. Charter is a tool (Law 6 — users, not an owner), but a tool INSTANCE needs a holder, and the holder is the one whose feedback loop can act on it. Codemonkey is the builder; build-quality feedback routes to the builder.
falsifier: RED if: (1) no charter tool instance exists under codemonkey at devices/codemonkey/0/tools/charter/0/; (2) a bus message addressed to 'charter' does not route to codemonkey's held instance; (3) the data_recorder instance on charter cannot receive feedback records; (4) the placement makes charter a machine — if it gates writes at its own address or gains glue that interfaces with its operation, the complexity axis was violated.
horizon: The sleep-state LLM reader that consumes the data_recorder is a separate ticket (scheduled-llm-gate-inspection); this ticket's scope ends at 'feedback can land and be read', not 'feedback is acted on'.

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — tester runs the proof: charter instance exists under codemonkey, bus routes to it, data_recorder instance can receive and be read
gates.kicks_back_on: red proof → route back to build

watchme.trigger: a probe fires feedback about charter quality and a record lands in codemonkey's held data_recorder instance
watchme.enough: at least one feedback record has been written to and read from the data_recorder instance
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier
watchme.consumer: scheduled-llm-gate-inspection (when built), or manual read in the interim

provenance: Akien session 2026-09-01: undelivered bus message surfaced that charter (a tool) has no receiver; discussion resolved that charter belongs under codemonkey because build-quality feedback belongs to the builder. First code ownership transfer from CC to another device — a milestone.
intent_berth: none, because this ticket was cast directly from conversation — the design was resolved in dialogue, not through /intent
owner: CC owns the code. Akien owns the design decision (codemonkey, not cairn).
traces_to: feedback-data-recorder — the tool this placement uses
Law 6 — tools have users, not owners; instances have holders
codemonkey charter — the device that receives ownership
